column1: # Mirror the Sloane Camera personnel-query flow: locate every employee
# who is not currently eligible for profit sharing.
# Wide viewport so column I (the PROFITSHARING field) is fully
# rendered for ASSERT_CELL — at the default 80×25 only the first
# ~3 characters of column I fit on-screen, so the assertions on the
# Layout (single-sheet — the tutorial uses worksheet B for the
# criteria range and worksheet C for the output range to protect the
# database from accidental overwrites; the L123 query semantics work
# the same whether the ranges live on the same sheet or different
# sheets, so this transcript stays single-sheet for tractability):
#   E1..E2   criteria range — single-field PROFITSHARING = No
#   G1..I5   output range — pre-filled header + room for matches
#   - /Data Query Input — POINT for the database, header row included.
#   - /Data Query Criteria — POINT for the criteria block.
#   - /Data Query Output — POINT for the destination block.
#   - /Data Query Find — pointer jumps to the first matching record.
#   - /Data Query Extract — copies all matching records into the
#     output range below its header, preserving input order.
#   - Field-name matching is case-insensitive and positional only by
#     name (not by column index), so the criteria range can name a
#     subset of the input fields in any order.
# --- Criteria range: PROFITSHARING field name in E1, criterion "No"
# in E2. The tutorial enters the criterion in lowercase to show that
# --- Output header in G1..I1. The tutorial copies the database's
# field names directly so extracted records line up under matching
# columns; only fields whose names appear in the output header are
# copied (Extract skips any input field absent from the output
# --- /Data Query — set Input, Criteria, Output, then Find.
# Input range A3..C8 — header row + records.
# Output range G1..I5 — header row + room for up to four matches.
# Find — pointer jumps to the first record where PROFITSHARING = No.
# That's Bird at A5 (Edwards/Atlanta/Yes at row 4 doesn't match).
# --- Extract — copy all matches into the output range.
# overflows column I's 9-char default width, so it's verified via the
# control-panel readout rather than the rendered cell.
# Matches in input order: Bird, Bjorkman, Percival.
# Row 5 in the output range stays blank — only three records matched,
# so the fourth slot is unused.
